Downtime-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Scheduled block-window marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general wellbeing guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Downtime workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Downtime vs App Limits phrasing

US pages use "Downtime", "Set Downtime", or "Bedtime lock." China storefront copy often uses 停用时间 for Apple's Downtime feature name under Screen Time settings, 就寝锁定 or 睡前锁定 when the gallery shows bedtime phone-lock flows, or 定时停用 when marketing emphasizes scheduled block windows — depending on whether you mean system Downtime setup or a third-party bedtime scheduler. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual marketing scope and avoids conflating Downtime with App Limits daily caps.

Downtime vs Focus modes and Sleep Focus

Downtime blocks most apps during a Screen Time schedule window — buyers searching for bedtime lock distinguish this from Focus mode profiles (专注模式) and Sleep Focus notification silencing. Match what your English listing and screenshots actually show.

停用时间 vs 屏幕使用时间

Apple's Chinese UI uses 停用时间 for Downtime under Screen Time and 屏幕使用时间 for the Screen Time settings hub and usage dashboards. Listing copy should pick the term buyers recognize on screenshots — a Downtime schedule frame needs 停用时间-friendly phrasing; a weekly usage chart frame belongs on the Screen Time guide, not here.

Allowed Apps vs Always Allowed

During Downtime, Allowed Apps (允许使用的 App) lists exceptions for the block window. Always Allowed (始终允许) covers apps and contacts that stay reachable outside Downtime restrictions. Use the term your screenshot actually shows — mixing them confuses buyers comparing your listing to iOS Settings labels.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Downtime-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 停用时间, 就寝锁定, and 定时停用 each signal different intent from App Limits, Focus mode, or generic parental-control keywords.
